v1.feedback: The upward RISE with no camera auto-follow means the active growth front drifts out of frame within ~60s — add a slow camera.target.y lerp toward the ribbon centroid. The crystallization pull (0.12 strength) reads too subtly as a tonal swerve at default zoom; amplify with a brief radial snap or scale discontinuity so the 'order imposed' moment is unmissable in 2s. The wireframe icosahedron would benefit from a slight emissive edge-glow or bloom pass to sell the divine-machine theatrics against the near-black field.

v2.feedback: The crystallization-snap mechanic genuinely delivers the 'deus-ex-machina' swerve — organic ribbon yanked into icosahedral order then released is theatrical and readable. Two fixes for a refinement: the ribbon starts as a thin 14-vertex ring that barely occupies the frame for the first 30+ seconds, so seed with more vertices or tighten the initial camera to keep the form above the 10% threshold from frame one. Second, the icosahedron wireframe descends with a simple sinusoidal bob — give it a more deliberate entrance (faster drop, brief hover, slow ascent) so the 'divine intervention' moment reads as a punctuation rather than a gentle pulse.
